A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DHG-Bench. Their complete main texts and appendices, including tables, figures and equations, are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, hyperedge-prediction, efficiency, robustness and fairness experiments in Tables 1–4 and Figures 2–5.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and adds experiments, reported in Table 1, Tables A5–A8, and the main-text and appendix figures.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a new learning algorithm. V2 expands the evaluated methods and documents package components more fully, but does not establish changes to the retained algorithms' learning procedures. HyperGT is an added existing comparator.

E1.justification: NTU2012 and ModelNet40 introduce a distinct 3D-object domain, increasing node-classification datasets from 11 to 13 and total datasets from 20 to 22. Perturbation testing also extends from Cora and Actor to Pubmed and Pokec. Existing datasets and the three prediction-task types remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds HyperGT, CEGCN and CEGAT to the reported comparisons. MLP, previously evaluated only for fairness, now also appears in node, hyperedge, hypergraph and efficiency comparisons. Within robustness experiments, PhenomNN and HyperGT expand the comparator set from eight to ten models.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 drops v1's specification of four validation/test sets with differing negative-sample difficulty and explicitly describes balanced mixed negative sampling for training, validation and testing. V2 also introduces fairness rankings averaged over executable datasets, requiring HNNs to run on at least two. Principal splits and task metrics remain unchanged; these reporting revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The six structural, feature and supervision perturbation analyses expand from two datasets and eight models to four datasets and ten models, with substantially revised feature-noise evidence. V2 additionally introduces the cross-dataset fairness-ranking analysis in Figure 5, rather than merely redisplaying the original fairness table.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-run averages and standard deviations. V2 explicitly specifies different random seeds for robustness repetitions and adds dispersion bars to the fairness-ranking summary, although their statistical definition is unspecified. No increase in replication or new significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive results for new datasets, comparators and robustness cases. Revised feature-noise curves reverse the reported noise-versus-masking ordering. Retained node and hyperedge scores are unchanged; small numerical revisions include ED-HNN's Bail demographic-parity gap changing from 8.08 to 8.05 and equalized-odds gap from 1.53 to 1.51 (Table 4 versus Table A8). Revised robustness results do not establish same-protocol performance gains.

T1.justification: The task definitions and fairness-disparity equations remain substantively unchanged. Appendix B.5 adds standard explanatory independence and equality statements for existing fairness metrics, without introducing new theory, assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a unified benchmark covering three task levels and four evaluation dimensions. Headline scope increases from 16 HNNs and 20 datasets to 17 HNNs and 22 datasets. The introduction's robustness takeaway now emphasizes feature perturbations alongside corrupted supervision.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of higher-order propagation versus MLP and clique-expansion baselines, spectral sensitivity to structural noise, and feature-noise saturation. Its robustness interpretation shifts toward structural resilience and stronger feature vulnerability. V1's explicit limitations concerning omitted tasks, unavailable methods and exclusion of self-supervised learning disappear; the relocated future directions do not preserve those qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 supplies Gaussian-noise calibration, perturbation grids and uniform label-flipping details absent from v1. Table A4 adds module-depth settings for ED-HNN and DPHGNN and attention settings for HyperGT. Graphics-data preprocessing and package modules receive new descriptions. Conversely, explicit MIT-license and maintenance/version-control statements are removed. Hardware and the repository address remain unchanged; added disclosure does not prove altered implementations.

R1.justification: V2 extends related-work discussion to TopoX and TopoBench and updates application, baseline and robustness references. It emphasizes the distinction between implementation toolkits and comprehensive quantitative evaluation, while retaining the original central positioning. THU-DH, renamed DHG, is the same cited work rather than a newly introduced predecessor.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, research-question descriptions and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Results gain standardized numbered observations and key-insight summaries. Future directions move into Appendix D.2, experimental appendices are reorganized, and a package section replaces the earlier reproducibility-section structure.

P2.justification: V1 Tables 2–4 move to Tables A6–A8, while node results are divided between Table 1 and Table A5. V2 adds a fairness-ranking chart, an algorithm timeline and three appendix robustness figures. The architecture diagram is redesigned as an appendix package diagram; dataset tables, plot styling, legends and boxed summaries also change substantially.

improvement.justification: Added MLP and clique-expansion baselines make effectiveness comparisons more informative, while broader robustness testing and explicit perturbation settings improve auditability. These gains are partly offset by removed limitations and licensing/maintenance disclosures. Numerical inconsistencies also remain: v2 Section 4.1.2 reports TF-HNN's DBLP-CA AP as 74.97, whereas Table A6 gives 74.69. The net benefit is supported but limited.
